newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice prices seen stable as demand lags.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice prices seen stable as demand lags.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are expected to remain stable next week with little demand seen from foreign buyers, dealers said on Thursday.
"We do not think prices will fluctuate widely," an official at the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) said.
There were some foreign buyers in the local market, but it was difficult to identify who, if anyone, was buying for Iraq after its oil-for-food deal with the U.N., he said.
Private exporters say Iraq had bought some rice from Pakistan but its quantity could not be immediately confirmed.

Javed Islam Agha, chairman of the Rice Exporters Association of Pakistan, said, "The association has no information about rice deals with Iraq. Some dealers on behalf of Iraq may have purchased 75,000 tonnes of rice in November and December."
The RECP official said the corporation had stopped export activities after the caretaker government said that it would be merged with the the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan.
The RECP sold its last stocks of 42,016 tonnes of IRRI-6 in an open auction at $238 per tonne CIF in the last week of December and had now stopped procuring rice from farmers.
The official said rice exports would now be left to the private sector.
Rice exports rose 59 percent to 116,980 tonnes worth $35 million in November from 73,593 worth $25 million in October.
